carouselA.title: What Fashion Owes Its Craftspeople: the institutional sequence

frames.caption: Fashion owes craftspeople more than romantic visibility: lawful and timely pay, safe conditions, credible credit, worker voice, remedy, preserved knowledge, and limits on extraction—specified for the actual relationship and jurisdiction.
frames.alt: Title plate for What Fashion Owes Its Craftspeople.
frames.treatment: typography, rule, folio and domain color only

frames.caption: Materials such as silk, glass, and metallic thread make skilled transformation visible while the museum record still names only the house as maker.

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 01 · NAME — Can the worker choose to be credited?. Build role-level credits with consent: cutter, embroiderer, weaver, dyer, machinist, finisher, presser, sample maker, repairer, and others as locally accurate. Protect people where naming creates risk.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping can the worker choose to be credited? within What Fashion Owes Its Craftspeople.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 02 · PAY — What commercial decisions reach the workroom?. Trace price, lead time, revisions, cancellations, overtime, payment schedule, subcontracting, and remedy. Purchasing decisions upstream can shape downstream labor outcomes; verify the actual chain.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what commercial decisions reach the workroom? within What Fashion Owes Its Craftspeople.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 03 · VOICE — Who can refuse, correct, and report harm?. Document worker-representation and grievance routes, anti-retaliation protections, safety escalation, correction of public credits, and who controls the response. A feedback form without remedy is not voice.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping who can refuse, correct, and report harm? within What Fashion Owes Its Craftspeople.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 04 · KNOWLEDGE — What does preservation return?. With consent, preserve process narration, terminology, samples, and contributor authority. Do not convert community knowledge into proprietary house content without permission, attribution, benefit, and cultural review.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what does preservation return? within What Fashion Owes Its Craftspeople.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.caption: Publicly naming craft can create recognition, but it may expose workers, simplify collective production, disclose confidential methods, or become reputation-washing. Credits, compensation, safety, bargaining, and cultural authority require separate mechanisms.
frames.alt: Counterpoint card for What Fashion Owes Its Craftspeople.
